itemsImport.title: Import Catalogue
itemsImport.subtitle: Add many items and their opening stock at once from an Excel or CSV file
itemsImport.templateHint: Download the template. Fill in the first sheet (Data), one row per item; the second sheet (Guide) explains what goes in every column. The opening-stock columns (lot, expiry, quantity, cost, supplier) can stay blank to add catalogue only. When done, upload the .xlsx or .csv file.
itemsImport.previewSummary: {valid} of {total} rows are ready to import. {errors} rows have a problem and will be skipped.

guide.title: How to fill in the catalogue import template
guide.intro: Fill in the "Data" sheet (the first sheet), one row per item. This "Guide" sheet is for reading only and is not imported.

how.1: One row is one new item. The import only adds items; existing items are never changed, and a code that is already in use is rejected.
how.2: Row 2 on the Data sheet is only an example. Delete or overwrite it before uploading, otherwise it is imported as an item too.
how.3: Do not change, delete or translate the column names in row 1. The system reads those names.
how.4: Only four columns are required to add an item: generic_name, form, unit and drug_class. Every other column may stay blank.
how.5: The last five columns (lot_number, expiry_date, qty, unit_cost, supplier) are opening stock. Leave them all blank to add the catalogue only. If you fill any one, expiry_date, qty and supplier become required.
how.6: A row can hold only one opening-stock batch. If an item has several batches, enter one here and record the rest through Receive stock.
how.7: Categories and suppliers must already exist under Categories and Suppliers (upper or lower case does not matter). A name that does not exist is rejected. If opening stock has no real supplier, use the "Saldo Awal" supplier.
how.8: Money is a plain number in rupiah: 15000, not Rp 15.000. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD: 2027-12-31, not 31/12/2027.
how.9: At most {max} rows per file. Rows with a problem are shown before you confirm and are skipped; the correct rows can still be imported. Save as .xlsx or .csv and upload; for .xlsx only the first sheet is read.

guide.classIntro: Write the code from the first column, exactly as shown (lower case).
guide.formIntro: Write the code from the first column, exactly as shown (lower case, in English). Not the name in the second column: "capsule", not "Kapsul".

requirement.batchRequired: Required if opening stock is filled in

classNote.keras: Red circle with the letter K. Returned items are not put back into stock.
classNote.owa: Pharmacy-only over-the-counter medicine (Obat Wajib Apotek). Returned items are not put back into stock.
classNote.psikotropika: A class recorded in the SIPNAP register. Returned items are not put back into stock.
classNote.narkotika: A class recorded in the SIPNAP register. Returned items are not put back into stock.
classNote.fitofarmaka: Herbal medicine that has passed clinical trials.
classNote.alkes: For example: blood pressure monitor, plasters, thermometer.
classNote.consumable: For example: cotton wool, syringes, gloves.

code.meaning: The item's code in this pharmacy. Leave blank to have one made from the generic name.
code.accepted: Letters and digits, no spaces. Must not match another item's code.

generic_name.meaning: The active ingredient, or the item's name.

brand_name.meaning: The brand name on the packaging, if any.

form.accepted: One of the codes in the dosage form list below, exactly as shown. Example: tablet, capsule, syrup.

strength.accepted: Free text. Example: 500 mg, 125 mg/5 mL

unit.meaning: The smallest unit that is counted and sold one at a time.
unit.accepted: Free text. Example: tablet, kapsul, botol, vial.

pack_size.meaning: How many units are in one box or pack, in the unit given in the unit column. Used to turn a number of boxes into units when receiving stock.
pack_size.accepted: A whole number, 1 or more. Example: 100 if a box holds 100 units.

category.accepted: The name of a category that already exists under Categories. Leave blank if uncategorised.

drug_class.meaning: The drug class as shown on the packaging.
drug_class.accepted: One of the codes in the drug class list below. Example: bebas, bebas_terbatas, keras.

nie.meaning: The BPOM marketing authorisation number (NIE). Needed if a product is recalled.
nie.accepted: Free text, exactly as on the packaging.

is_tax_exempt.meaning: Mark if this item is exempt from PPN.
is_tax_exempt.accepted: yes or no. Also read as yes: 1, y, ya, true. Blank or anything else means not exempt.

reorder_point.meaning: The minimum stock level. The low-stock alert appears at this quantity.
reorder_point.accepted: A whole number, 0 or more. Blank is read as 0.

reorder_qty.accepted: A whole number, 1 or more. May be blank.

default_price.meaning: Selling price per unit, in rupiah.
default_price.accepted: A plain number with no Rp, dots or commas. Example: 12000. Blank is read as 0.

min_shelf_life_days.meaning: The shortest remaining shelf life (in days) that may be accepted when stock arrives.
min_shelf_life_days.accepted: A whole number, 0 or more. May be blank.

barcode.accepted: Exactly as printed; do not drop leading zeros. Must not match another item's barcode.

lot_number.meaning: Opening stock: the lot number as printed on the packaging.
lot_number.accepted: Text. May be blank if it is really not known.

expiry_date.meaning: Opening stock: the batch's expiry date.
expiry_date.accepted: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2027-12-31. Must not have passed; expired stock is rejected.

qty.meaning: Opening stock: how many units of this batch are on hand now, in units.

unit_cost.meaning: Opening stock: purchase price per unit, in rupiah.
unit_cost.accepted: A plain number with no Rp, dots or commas. Example: 9000. Blank is read as 0.

supplier.meaning: Opening stock: the supplier of this batch.
supplier.accepted: The name of a supplier that already exists under Suppliers. If unknown, use Saldo Awal.

receive.title: Receive stock
receive.subtitle: Book in a delivery with its lot number and expiry date
receive.scanHint: Scan the barcode and press Enter. A GS1 code fills in the lot and expiry too.
receive.scanUnknown: Barcode not on file. Pick the item below and this code will be saved with it.
receive.scanUnreadable: That barcode could not be read.
receive.legacyHint: Only for old stock from paper records. The expiry date is still required.
receive.expiryHint: Boxes usually print only a month and year.
receive.costPerPack: Per pack. The per-unit cost is worked out for you.
receive.openingHint: For stock already on the shelf when the system starts, rather than a new purchase.
receive.needItems: The catalogue is empty. Add items before booking in a delivery.

stock.noBatches: No stock recorded for this item yet.

sell.title: Sell
sell.subtitle: Point of sale and dispensing
sell.searchHint: Type a name or code, or scan a barcode, then press Enter.
sell.expiredOnly: All {qty} units have expired and cannot be sold.
sell.emptyBasket: The basket is empty. Search or scan an item to begin.
sell.searchHintNoScan: Type a name or code, then press Enter.
sell.scanAim: Hold the barcode inside the frame.
sell.scanTypeInstead: You can still type the name or the code into the search box.
sell.scanUnsupported: This browser cannot read barcodes with the camera.
sell.scanDenied: Camera access was refused. Allow it in the browser's site settings, and note that the camera only works over https or on this machine.
sell.scanNoCamera: No camera was found on this device.
sell.scanInsecure: The camera is blocked because this page is not on https. Open the till over https, or over localhost on this machine.
sell.scanFailed: The camera could not be started.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.subtitle: Out of stock, running low, and approaching expiry
alerts.none: Nothing to act on. Stock is in good shape.
alerts.expiredUnitsOnShelf: {qty} expired units still on the shelf

dashboard.noSalesYet: No sales in this period yet.

returns.title: Return
returns.subtitle: Take stock back against sale {number}
returns.listSubtitle: Everything that has come back over the counter
returns.quarantineNotice: Returned medicine goes to quarantine, not back on the shelf. Once a box has left the counter nobody knows how it was stored.
returns.restockNotice: Sealed over-the-counter stock goes back to its batch. Obat keras, OWA, psikotropika and narkotika are quarantined regardless of this setting.
returns.nothingReturnable: Every unit on this sale has already come back.

dispose.title: Disposal
dispose.subtitle: Write expired and quarantined stock off the shelf
dispose.queueEmpty: Nothing is waiting to be written off.
dispose.historyEmpty: Nothing has been written off yet.
dispose.methodPlaceholder: For example: incinerated, returned to supplier
dispose.confirmBody: A disposal is permanent and stays in the record forever. Check the lot number and the quantity against what is in your hand.
dispose.totalLoss: Written off in the last 30 days

counts.title: Stock count
counts.subtitle: Count the shelf, then post what you found
counts.newSubtitle: This writes down what the system believes right now, so you can compare it with the shelf
counts.name: What to call this count
counts.categoryHint: Counting one category at a time is far less disruptive than closing.
counts.freezeWarning: Stock should not move while a category is being counted. Anything sold mid-count still lands in the ledger, but the sheet will disagree with the shelf.
counts.noVariances: The shelf and the record agree.
counts.postHint: Posting turns every difference into an adjustment in the ledger, with your reason attached.
counts.printHint: Print, count with a pen, then type the numbers in.
counts.explainFirst: Every difference needs a reason before the count can be posted.

reports.title: Reports
reports.subtitle: Sales, profit, stock and losses, for any period
reports.exportHint: The main table as CSV, for Google Sheets or anything else. Amounts are plain numbers so they can be summed.

blurb.sales: The sales summary, the daily trend, busy hours, and detail by item, category, cashier and payment method
blurb.movements: Every unit in and every unit out, per product, with who recorded it
blurb.margin: Net sales against their cost, by item and by category
blurb.valuation: What is on the shelf right now, at cost
blurb.expiry: What was written off, and why
blurb.suppliers: What each supplier delivered, and how much of it was binned

sales.voidedHint: Excluded from every figure on this page
sales.dailyNote: The value of each day's transactions, before returns.
sales.byPaymentNote: Money in by payment method, less refunds paid back by that method. Check it against the cash count and the bank statement.
sales.byHourNote: Till transactions per hour of the day. Imported history has no time of day.
sales.byItemNote: ABC classes: A = the items that together make 80% of sales ({a} items), B = the next 15% ({b}), C = the rest ({c}). Never let an A item run out.
sales.byCashierNote: The value of the transactions each person served, VAT included, before returns.
sales.voidedLine: {count} sales were voided in this period and are left out of every figure.

movements.note: Open a product to see every movement behind its totals: what came in, what went out, when, and who recorded it.
movements.truncated: There are more movements in this period than the screen lists. The totals are complete; the lists below show the most recent ones. Download the CSV for every row.
movements.listTruncated: Older movements for this product are not listed here. Choose it above, shorten the period, or download the CSV.

margin.costNote: Cost is what each batch actually cost when it was sold, copied onto the sale at the time. A later delivery at a different price does not change a past month's margin.
margin.netOfReturns: Returned units take back both their price and their cost.
margin.marginLine: {percent} margin on net sales. Previous period ({period}): {previous}.
margin.howTitle: How these figures are worked out
margin.netOfDiscount: Net sales are after discounts and exclude VAT, so profit never looks bigger than it is.
margin.lossMakers: {count} items sold below their cost. Sort the Gross profit column to see them.
margin.uncosted: Imported history worth {revenue} has no cost, so it is left out of this report. Fill in unit_cost when importing to include it.

valuation.nowOnly: This is a snapshot of the shelf right now. A valuation for a past date would mean replaying the ledger, which this report does not do.
valuation.expiredWarning: Expired stock still counted here is money already lost. Write it off from the Disposal screen.
valuation.quarantineNote: Quarantined and expired batches are included: the money is still tied up in them.
valuation.soonHint: Sell it first, or return it to the supplier while you still can.
valuation.sellableNote: Sellable stock only. Quarantined and expired batches are in the other table.

expiry.note: Valued at what each batch cost, snapshotted when it was destroyed.

suppliers.note: The last column is the one worth watching. Stock that arrives close to its expiry is not cheap, whatever the invoice says.

reports.importHistoryBlurb: Bring in sales from before this system, so the reports can look back
reports.overviewExpiryLoss: Stock worth {value} was written off in this period. See Expiry loss.
reports.exportXlsxHint: An Excel workbook: a summary sheet and one sheet per table, with figures that sum as they are.

statement.title: Sales summary
statement.note: From the prices charged to the money actually kept.

history.included: Includes imported sales history: {revenue} from {lines} lines.
history.withoutReceipt: {count} lines without a receipt number are not counted as transactions.

users.title: Accounts
users.subtitle: Who can sign in, and what each of them may do
users.usernameHint: Lowercase letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore.
users.fullNameHint: As it should appear on the audit log and on receipts.
users.noPermissions: No permissions yet — this account can sign in and see nothing.
users.pharmacistHint: Required to be recorded as responsible for obat keras, and for the narkotika register later.
users.templateHint: A starting point, not a fixed role. Adjust the boxes below before saving.
users.permissionsHint: Hiding a screen is a courtesy; these are the control. Every action checks them on the server.
users.sensitiveWarning: This gives access to cost prices, accounts or settings. Grant it deliberately.
users.passwordBody: Write this down and hand it over now. It is shown once and cannot be recovered — only replaced. {name} must set their own password before anything else will load.
users.passwordDone: I have given it to them
users.resetHint: Signs the account out everywhere and clears any lockout.
users.suspendHint: Signs them out immediately. Nothing is deleted; the account can be brought back.
users.ownerNotice: The owner holds every permission and cannot be suspended. If this account is locked out, recovery is a command on the machine the database runs on.
users.cannotEditOwn: You cannot suspend your own account.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: How the pharmacy works, and what it shows
settings.businessNameHint: Printed at the top of every receipt.
settings.npwpHint: Only needed once the business is a PKP.
settings.receiptLocaleHint: A business decision, not the cashier's. A cashier working in English must not hand an Indonesian customer an English receipt.
settings.timezoneHint: Decides when a day starts, which decides when a batch expires and which day a sale belongs to.
settings.modulesHint: This decides what staff are shown, not what they are allowed to do. Permissions remain the control, and nothing already recorded is hidden.

module.returnsHint: Taking medicine back over the counter. Off hides the returns screen and the button on a sale.
module.barcodesHint: The scan fields on receiving and at the till. Worth leaving off until a scanner is plugged in.
module.taxHint: Off means no tax fields anywhere and a plain nota. A pharmacy below the PKP threshold does not charge PPN.
module.narkotikaHint: Switch on the day you first stock them. Items already carrying these classes keep showing them either way.
module.suppliersHint: Supplier records and the picker on receiving. Off hides the Suppliers screen from the menu.
module.categoriesHint: Item categories, for organizing and filtering the catalogue. Off hides the Categories screen from the menu.
module.countsHint: Physical counts and posting the difference found. Off hides the Counts screen from the menu.
module.disposeHint: Recording expired or damaged stock as a loss. Off hides the Dispose screen from the menu.
module.importHint: The Import button on the Catalogue screen. Who may actually use it is still controlled by the "Import catalogue" permission per account.

settings.taxRateHistoryHint: Old rates are kept, never edited: a receipt reprinted from last year must still show the rate that applied on the day.
settings.noEffectiveRate: PPN is switched on but no rate covers today, so sales are being recorded with no PPN at all. Add a rate below.
settings.alertsHint: In days. Expired stock and out-of-stock are not thresholds — they are facts, and they always alert.
settings.allowRestock: Allow sealed stock back on the shelf
settings.allowRestockHint: Applies to over-the-counter items and devices only. Obat keras, OWA, psikotropika and narkotika are always quarantined, whatever this says.
settings.restricted: Only the owner can change these.
settings.businessTaglineHint: The line under the name, on the sidebar and the sign-in screen. Describe the pharmacy, not the software.
settings.timezoneMismatch: This machine is set to {zone}. If that is where the pharmacy is, change this to match — an hour's difference moves a sale into the wrong day.
settings.digestHint: One email each morning with yesterday's takings and anything that needs attention before opening.
settings.digestEnabledHint: Nothing is sent until this is on and a mail server is configured below.
settings.digestHourHint: Local time. The job runs once a day; it does not send twice for the same day.
settings.digestPreviewOnly: No mail server is configured, so the digest is written to a file instead of sent. You can read it before deciding to switch sending on.
settings.mailHint: Used only for the daily digest. Leave it blank and the digest is written to a file you can open in a browser.
settings.smtpHostHint: For a Gmail address this is smtp.gmail.com, and the password is an app password rather than your own.
settings.smtpPasswordHint: Stored on the server and never shown again.
settings.smtpPasswordStored: A password is stored. Leave blank to keep it; type a new one to replace it.
settings.smtpFromHint: The address the email appears to come from. Most servers require it to be one you own.
settings.smtpSecureHint: On for port 465. Port 587 upgrades the connection itself and does not need this.
settings.mailTestHint: Connects and signs in without sending anything. Tests what is saved, so save first.
settings.mailFailed: Could not connect or sign in.
settings.demoHint: This install still holds the sample pharmacy: {items} items, {batches} batches and {sales} sales, so staff can learn the till first. Clear it before you enter your own items: clearing empties the whole catalogue, including anything you added.
settings.demoWiped: Demo data cleared. The catalogue, stock and history are empty; accounts and settings are untouched.
settings.demoKeeps: Accounts, permissions, settings, tax rates and the audit log all survive. Items, stock, the ledger, sales, returns, disposals, counts and alerts do not.

items.import: Import the catalogue from a spreadsheet

sales.price_override: Change a price at the till
sales.batch_override: Choose a batch other than the earliest
sales.view_all: See everyone's sales, not only their own

reports.financial: See cost prices, margins and stock value

prompt.title: New here?
prompt.body: A short tour that shows you on the real screens where everything is and how to use it. About five minutes, and nothing is saved.

intro.title: Welcome
intro.owner: This walkthrough covers every screen in the pharmacy system, since your account holds every permission. You can reopen it any time from this button.
intro.staff: This walkthrough only covers the screens set up for your account -- if something you use is missing here, ask the owner about your permissions. You can reopen it any time from this button.
intro.partial: This walkthrough shows the screens for this guide, one part at a time. It skips anything your account cannot use.

chapters.dashboard: The first screen after signing in. It shows at a glance what needs attention today.
chapters.sell: Where you serve customers: find the medicine, put it in the basket, take the payment. Expired medicine is refused automatically.
chapters.items: Every medicine you sell, with its price and how much is left.
chapters.receive: Used whenever a delivery arrives from a supplier, so the stock goes up.
chapters.sales: Every sale made so far, with its receipt.
chapters.returns: Medicine brought back by customers. Returned medicine is kept apart, not simply sold again.
chapters.dispose: For recording damaged or expired medicine thrown away from the shelf.
chapters.counts: For recounting the shelf and matching it against the system.
chapters.alerts: What needs doing: medicine running low, close to expiry, or already expired.
chapters.suppliers: The suppliers the pharmacy buys from.
chapters.categories: Groups of medicines, such as Antibiotics or Vitamins, to keep lists and reports tidy.
chapters.reports: Sales, stock and profit for a period you choose.
chapters.users: An account for each member of staff, and what each may do.
chapters.settings: The pharmacy's name, tax, receipts and which features are in use.

outro.title: That's everything
outro.body: You can come back to this walkthrough any time using the Tutorial button.

tour.how: The screen dims and the part being explained lights up. Sometimes you will be asked to click or type yourself. Nothing is saved during the tutorial.
tour.clickMenu: Click the lit-up entry in the menu to open it.

try.type: Try it now: type in the lit-up field. The tutorial moves on once the result appears.
try.click: Try it now: click what is lit up. The tutorial moves on by itself.

summary.title: Stock summary
summary.body: Four numbers to check every morning: expired medicine still on the shelf, medicine that has run out, medicine expiring soon, and medicine running low. Ideally all zero.

sales.title: Sales
sales.body: Today's takings and number of sales, and a 30-day chart to see busy and quiet days.

catalogue.title: Catalogue
catalogue.body: How many medicines, categories and suppliers are recorded. Click one to open its list.

search.title: 1. Find the medicine
search.body: Type a name or code, for example "para" for Paracetamol. With a barcode scanner, just scan the box; on a phone the camera button scans too.

results.title: 2. Pick it
results.body: Each result shows the stock left and the price. Click one to put it in the basket. Medicine that has run out or expired cannot be picked.

qty.title: 3. Set the quantity
qty.body: Press + or −, or type the number. If it is more than is in stock, the till says so and the sale cannot be completed.

lot.title: The lot going out
lot.body: The batch number and expiry that will be taken. The system always takes the one expiring soonest first, so check it against the box in your hand.

summary.title: 4. Check the total
summary.body: Subtotal, discount (if your account may give one), and the total to pay.

pay.title: 5. Payment
pay.body: Choose how the customer pays: cash, card, QRIS or transfer.

tendered.title: 6. Cash received
tendered.body: For cash, type what the customer handed over, for example 50000. The change is worked out straight away.

checkout.title: 7. Complete the sale
checkout.body: This saves the sale, takes the stock off the shelf and opens the receipt to print. Do not press it during the tutorial. This practice basket disappears when you leave the screen.

search.title: Search and filter
search.body: Find a medicine by name, code or NIE number, or filter by category and class, then press Search.

list.title: Medicines
list.body: One row per medicine, with its class, category, stock left, selling price and minimum stock level.

class.title: Drug class mark
class.body: The same as on the packaging: green circle for over-the-counter, blue for limited OTC, red with a K for prescription-only.

stock.title: Stock left
stock.body: What can still be sold, added up across every batch. Nobody types this number; it changes by itself as stock is received, sold, returned or disposed of.

open.title: Open a medicine
open.body: Click a name to see its details.

batches.title: Its batches
batches.body: Each delivery is one batch with its own number, expiry date and quantity left. Expired or quarantined batches are never sold.

movements.title: Stock history
movements.body: Every unit in and out: when, by whom and why -- delivery, sale, return, disposal or count. This history cannot be edited or deleted.

add.title: Add medicines
add.body: Back on the list: add a new medicine one at a time, or import many at once from an Excel file.

scan.title: Scan the box
scan.body: If the box has a GS1 barcode, scan it here: the medicine, batch number and expiry fill themselves in.

item.title: Which medicine?
item.body: Choose the medicine that arrived. If it is not in the list yet, add it under Items first.

supplier.title: From whom?
supplier.body: Choose the supplier. "Saldo Awal" is only for stock already on the shelf when the system started.

lot.title: Batch number
lot.body: Copy it off the packaging, usually marked "Batch" or "Lot". It is what a recall is traced by.

expiry.title: Expiry date
expiry.body: Required. Packaging usually shows only the month and year: pick the month and type the year.

quantity.title: Quantity
quantity.body: How many arrived, in the smallest unit (tablets, capsules) or in packs. The system works out the contents.

cost.title: Purchase price
cost.body: What you paid per unit or per pack, from the invoice. Used to work out profit in the reports.

opening.title: Opening stock
opening.body: Tick only when entering stock already on the shelf when the system started, never for a new purchase.

save.title: Save
save.body: Once saved, the stock goes up straight away and the delivery appears below under today's deliveries.

list.title: Every sale
list.body: One row per receipt: number, time, cashier, payment, total and status.

open.title: Open a receipt
open.body: Click a receipt number to see it.

receipt.title: The receipt
receipt.body: The sale exactly as printed for the customer, including the batch of every medicine.

print.title: Reprint
print.body: If the customer asks for the receipt again, print it from here.

return.title: Return
return.body: If a customer brings medicine back, start the return here. It is kept apart and not simply sold again.

void.title: Void the sale
void.body: For a sale entered by mistake. A reason is required, every unit goes back on the shelf, and the receipt stays on record as voided.

list.title: Returns
list.body: Every return, with its reason and the refund. A return is started from its receipt in Sales history.

queue.title: Waiting for disposal
queue.body: Expired medicine and quarantined returns appear here. Click Dispose to record throwing it away.

history.title: Disposal history
history.body: Everything disposed of and the total loss. This is how you see which medicines are being over-ordered.

start.title: Start a stock count
start.body: Start a new count, of every shelf or one category.

list.title: Earlier counts
list.body: Every stock count is kept here with its status.

lines.title: Count results
lines.body: Per batch: what the system expected, what was really on the shelf, and the difference with its reason. Posting books the difference.

filter.title: Filter alerts
filter.body: Show only one kind or level of alert.

list.title: Alerts
list.body: The most urgent are always at the top.

first.title: One alert
first.body: Red means urgent: out of stock, or expired medicine still on the shelf. Amber means reorder soon or expiring soon.

actions.title: Follow up
actions.body: Mark it handled (for example, already ordered) or snooze it for a few days. Red alerts cannot be snoozed.

refresh.title: Refresh
refresh.body: Alerts are checked automatically every day. Press this to check now.

list.title: Suppliers
list.body: Saved suppliers are offered when you receive stock.

add.title: Add a supplier
add.body: Enter the name, a contact person and a phone number.

list.title: Categories
list.body: Categories group medicines in the catalogue, in stock counts and in reports.

range.title: Choose a period
range.body: Pick the dates: today, the last 7, 30 or 90 days, this month, last month, or your own. Every figure is compared with the period before.

pick.title: Open a report
pick.body: Click a report, for example Sales.

tabs.title: Switch report
tabs.body: Jump to another report without going back to the list.

result.title: Results
result.body: The figures for the chosen period. The stock card report is how you check what left the shelf against what was rung up.

export.title: Print and download
export.body: Print the report on A4, or download it as Excel (one sheet per table) or CSV to send to the accountant.

add.title: Create an account
add.body: One account per member of staff, never shared. The temporary password is shown only once, and they change it at first sign-in.

list.title: Accounts
list.body: Click an account to change what it may do, reset its password or suspend it.

business.title: Pharmacy details
business.body: The pharmacy's name, address and timezone. The name appears in the menu, on the sign-in screen and on receipts.

receipt.title: Receipt
receipt.body: The receipt language and the note printed at its foot, such as a get-well message.

modules.title: Features
modules.body: Switch off screens you do not use to keep the menu short. Anything already recorded stays safe.

alerts.title: Alert thresholds
alerts.body: How many days before expiry a medicine starts being flagged.

demo.title: Demo data
demo.body: All the sample medicines, stock and sales. Clear them here before entering your own items, because clearing empties the whole catalogue. Accounts and settings stay.

guides.title: Tutorials
guides.subtitle: Step-by-step guides for the work your account does
guides.notListed: Only the guides for what your account may do are listed. If you need a job that is not here, ask the owner to check your permissions.
guides.showMeHint: Lights up the real screens one part at a time. Nothing is saved.
guides.fullTourHint: Every screen in your menu, one after another, in about five minutes.

start.title: Getting started
start.summary: Signing in, finding your way around, and the few rules the system never bends.

signIn.title: Signing in the first time

steps.1: The owner gives you a username and a temporary password. It is shown to them only once, so write it down when they hand it over.
steps.2: Open the pharmacy system in the browser and sign in with them.
steps.3: You are asked to set your own password straight away. Nothing else opens until you do.
steps.4: Choose something only you know. The owner never sees it -- that is what lets every sale be credited to the person who really made it.

signIn.tip: Forgot your password? Nobody can look it up, not even the owner. Ask them to issue a new temporary one and you will set a fresh password again.

menu.title: Finding your way around

steps.1: The menu on the left only lists the screens your account may use, grouped under Selling, Stock, Reports & records and Administration.
steps.2: The purple Open the till button at the top is where you serve customers. It is the screen most people use all day.
steps.3: Hover over a menu entry to read what that screen is for.
steps.4: On a computer, the arrow at the top of the menu shrinks it to icons for more room. On a phone the menu is tucked away behind the ☰ button.
steps.5: The Tutorial button at the bottom of the menu brings you back to these guides at any time. Sign out is next to it.

menu.tip: The system works in the language set on your account. To change it, ask the owner.

steps.1: After signing in you land on the dashboard.
steps.2: The four numbers at the top are the ones to check every morning: expired medicine still on the shelf, medicine that has run out, medicine expiring soon, and medicine running low.
steps.3: Below them are today's takings and a chart of the last 30 days, and the size of the catalogue.
steps.4: Click a number to open the alerts or the list behind it.

alerts.title: The alert count in the menu

steps.1: The number next to Alerts in the menu tells you how many things need doing.
steps.2: Red means something urgent: stock has run out, or expired medicine is still on the shelf.
steps.3: Amber means something to plan for: reorder soon, or expiring soon.
steps.4: See the Alerts guide for what to do about each one.

rules.title: Rules the system never bends

steps.1: Expired medicine cannot be sold. The till refuses it, and no permission can override that.
steps.2: Nothing is ever deleted. Sales are voided, items are archived, accounts are suspended -- and the record of what happened stays.
steps.3: Every change is recorded under the name of the person who made it. Never share an account or sign in for someone else.
steps.4: Stock is never typed in by hand. It goes up when a delivery is received and down when medicine is sold, returned to quarantine or written off.

rules.warn: If the system refuses something, it is usually protecting a patient or the records. Ask the owner or pharmacist rather than looking for a way around it.

steps.1: Pick the guide for the job you are about to do from the Tutorials page.
steps.2: Each guide has a "Show me on screen" button that walks you through the real screens without saving anything.
steps.3: The demo pharmacy that comes with a new install is safe to practise on until the owner clears it.

setup.title: Setting up the pharmacy
setup.summary: For the owner: the order to do things in when the pharmacy starts using the system for real.

demo.title: 1. Clear the demo data -- first, not last

steps.1: A new install comes with a sample pharmacy so staff can practise on the till.
steps.2: When you are ready to go live, open Settings and scroll to Demo data at the bottom.
steps.3: Type the confirmation phrase and press Clear the demo data.
steps.4: Accounts, permissions, settings, tax rates and the audit log stay. Items, stock, sales and everything else built on them are emptied.

demo.warn: Clearing empties the whole catalogue, including anything you added yourself. Do it before you enter your real medicines, never after.

steps.1: In Settings, fill in the name, description, address, phone and licence number. The name appears in the menu, on the sign-in screen and at the top of every receipt.
steps.2: Check the timezone. It decides when a day starts, which decides which day a sale belongs to and the exact day a batch expires.
steps.3: Choose the receipt language and the line printed at its foot.
steps.4: Switch off features you will not use, and set PPN only if your accountant says the pharmacy charges it.

lists.title: 3. Categories and suppliers

steps.1: Add the categories you want to group medicines by, for example Antibiotics, Vitamins, Analgesics.
steps.2: Add the suppliers (PBF) you buy from, with a contact person and phone number.

lists.tip: Do these before the medicines: the item form and the delivery form pick from these lists.

steps.1: Add each medicine under Items → Add item, or many at once with Import.
steps.2: For an import, download the template, fill in the Data sheet (the Guide sheet explains every column) and upload it. A row can carry the stock already on the shelf too, with its batch number and expiry.
steps.3: An item holds no stock of its own. It shows zero until stock is received against it.

opening.title: 5. Enter what is already on the shelf

steps.1: For each medicine on the shelf, open Receive stock.
steps.2: Enter the batch number and expiry printed on the box, and the quantity you counted.
steps.3: Tick Opening stock. This marks it as stock you already had, not a new purchase.
steps.4: If the batch number of old stock is unknown, tick Lot number unknown -- the expiry date is still required.

opening.warn: Opening stock is only for the first day. Every delivery after that is a normal delivery with Opening stock left unticked.

steps.1: Under Accounts, create one account per person. Never a shared one.
steps.2: Start from the Cashier, Stock clerk or Manager template and adjust the boxes.
steps.3: Hand each person their temporary password. They set their own at first sign-in.

count.title: 7. Check it with a count

steps.1: Once the opening stock is in, run a stock count category by category.
steps.2: Any difference shows you a box that was missed or mistyped, and posting the count corrects it with a reason on record.

count.tip: From here, the Tutorials page shows each member of staff only the guides for what their account can do.

cashier.title: Working the till
cashier.summary: Serving a customer from start to finish: finding the medicine, the batch, the payment and the receipt.

open.title: Opening the till

steps.1: Press the purple Open the till button at the top of the menu.
steps.2: The cursor is already in the search box, so you can type or scan straight away.
steps.3: Each sale is recorded under your name. If someone else takes over the counter, they sign in with their own account.

open.tip: Leave the till open all day. A new sale starts as soon as the last one is completed.

find.title: 1. Find the medicine

steps.1: Type part of the name or the code, for example "para" for Paracetamol, and press Enter.
steps.2: With a barcode scanner, just scan the box. The search box reads it like typing.
steps.3: On a phone or tablet, the camera button scans the barcode too.
steps.4: Each result shows the stock left and the price. Click the right one to put it in the basket.

find.tip: If nothing is found, try the generic name instead of the brand, or fewer letters. If it really is missing, the medicine has not been added to the catalogue yet -- tell whoever manages stock.

basket.title: 2. Set the quantity

steps.1: Press + or −, or type the number in the quantity box.
steps.2: The quantity is in the smallest unit: tablets, capsules, bottles.
steps.3: To sell several medicines, search again and add each one. Press Remove on a line that was picked by mistake.

basket.warn: If you ask for more than is in stock, the till says so and the sale cannot be completed. Medicine that has run out or expired cannot be added at all.

batch.title: 3. Check the batch

steps.1: Under each line the till shows which batch is going out and its expiry date.
steps.2: It always picks the batch that expires soonest, so older stock leaves first.
steps.3: Take the box with that batch number off the shelf and check that it matches.

batch.tip: If the box in your hand is from a different batch, the shelf is out of order: put the soonest-expiring box at the front.

steps.1: Your account may choose a batch other than the soonest-expiring one.
steps.2: Open the batch list on the line and pick the one you are handing over.
steps.3: Type a short reason, for example "customer needs a later expiry". It is kept with the sale.

steps.1: Your account may change the unit price on a line.
steps.2: Only do so when the owner's price list says so. The change is recorded with the sale under your name.

steps.1: Type the discount amount in rupiah in the Discount field under the subtotal.
steps.2: The total updates straight away. The discount cannot be more than the subtotal.

steps.1: Check the total with the customer.
steps.2: Choose how they pay: cash, debit card, credit card, QRIS, bank transfer or other.
steps.3: For cash, type what the customer handed over, for example 50000 or 50.000. The change to give back appears straight away.

finish.title: 5. Complete the sale

steps.1: Press Complete sale. The stock comes off the shelf and the receipt number appears.
steps.2: Press View receipt and print it for the customer.
steps.3: Press New sale, or just start typing, to serve the next customer.

finish.tip: The receipt shows the batch of every medicine. If there is ever a recall, that is how the pharmacy finds who received it.

classes.title: Drug class marks

steps.1: Each medicine shows the same mark as its packaging.
steps.2: Green circle: Obat Bebas, over the counter.
steps.3: Blue circle: Obat Bebas Terbatas, over the counter with a warning.
steps.4: Red circle with K: Obat Keras and other prescription medicines.

classes.warn: The till does not check prescriptions for you. Obat keras, psikotropika and narkotika follow the pharmacist's rules -- when in doubt, call the pharmacist before selling.

mistakes.title: When something goes wrong

steps.1: Before pressing Complete sale, nothing is saved. Remove the wrong line or leave the till and start again.
steps.2: After it is completed, a sale is never deleted. A mistake is voided, and a customer bringing medicine back is a return.
steps.3: If your account cannot void or take returns, call whoever can, and give them the receipt number.

mistakes.warn: Never ring up a new sale to cancel out a wrong one. The stock and the takings would both end up wrong.

steps.1: Open Sales history in the menu to see earlier receipts.
steps.2: Click a receipt number to see it and reprint it if the customer asks.
steps.3: Unless your account may see everyone's, the list only shows the sales you made.

returns.title: Voids and returns
returns.summary: Undoing a sale entered by mistake, and taking medicine back from a customer.

which.title: Void or return?

steps.1: Void: the sale should never have happened -- wrong item, wrong quantity, rung up twice. Every unit goes back to its batch as if it never left.
steps.2: Return: the sale was real, and the customer has brought some or all of it back later.
steps.3: Both start from the receipt: open Sales history and click the receipt number.

which.tip: The medicine never left the counter? Void. It went home with the customer? Return.

void.title: Voiding a sale

steps.1: Open the receipt from Sales history.
steps.2: Press Void sale and type the reason, for example "rung up twice".
steps.3: Confirm. The receipt stays on record marked as voided, with your name and the reason, and the stock goes back.
steps.4: Voided sales are left out of every sales figure.

void.warn: A sale that has already had a return cannot be voided -- the returned units would be booked back twice. The void button disappears once there is a return.

steps.1: Open the receipt the medicine was sold on, and press Process a return.
steps.2: For each line, enter how many units are coming back. You cannot return more than was sold, or more than has not already come back.
steps.3: Write why it is coming back, for example "wrong dose dispensed".
steps.4: Choose how the refund is paid. The refund is worked out from what the customer actually paid, discount included.
steps.5: Press Record the return and give the customer the refund.

quarantine.title: Where returned medicine goes

steps.1: Returned medicine goes to quarantine, not back on the shelf. Once a box has left the counter, nobody knows how it was kept.
steps.2: Obat keras, OWA, psikotropika and narkotika are always quarantined.
steps.3: Sealed over-the-counter stock can go back on sale only if the owner has switched that on in Settings.

quarantine.warn: Put the returned box aside, away from the shelf. Quarantined stock is written off from the Disposal screen.

steps.1: The Returns screen lists every return with its reason, the refund and who took it.
steps.2: The receipt also shows the returns made against it.

delivery.title: When a delivery arrives
delivery.summary: Booking in a new batch from a supplier so the stock goes up -- and doing it so a recall can be traced.

before.title: Before you start

steps.1: Check the boxes against the supplier's invoice: the right medicines, the right quantities, nothing damaged.
steps.2: Check the expiry date on every batch. Refuse medicine that is expired or expires too soon, before it is booked in.
steps.3: Make sure each medicine already exists under Items. A new medicine has to be added to the catalogue first -- see the guide for new medicines.

before.warn: Book in each batch number separately. Two batches of the same medicine have different expiry dates, and mixing them means the wrong one is sold first.

scan.title: Scanning the box

steps.1: Open Receive stock in the menu and put the cursor in the scan field.
steps.2: Scan the barcode and press Enter.
steps.3: A GS1 barcode (the square or long one with batch and expiry inside) fills in the medicine, the batch number and the expiry by itself.
steps.4: If the barcode is not on file yet, pick the medicine below and the code is saved with it, so it is recognised next time.

scan.tip: Always check what the scan filled in against the printing on the box.

steps.1: Choose the medicine that arrived.
steps.2: Choose the supplier. "Saldo Awal" is only for stock that was already on the shelf when the system started.
steps.3: Check the date received. It is today unless you are booking in yesterday's delivery late.

lot.title: 2. The batch number

steps.1: Copy it off the packaging exactly. It is usually marked "Batch", "Lot" or "No. Bets".
steps.2: Only for old stock from paper records with no batch number, tick Lot number unknown.

lot.tip: The batch number is what a BPOM recall names. Getting it right is what lets the pharmacy find every box and every customer.

expiry.title: 3. The expiry date

steps.1: Required for every batch.
steps.2: Boxes usually print only a month and a year: pick the month and type the year, for example 2027.
steps.3: The batch is treated as expired from the end of that month.

expiry.warn: Read it twice. A wrong expiry means medicine is either sold after it expires or thrown away while it is still good.

quantity.title: 4. Quantity and cost

steps.1: Enter how many arrived. Switch between units (tablets, capsules) and packs -- in packs, the system works out the units from the pack size.
steps.2: Enter the cost price from the invoice, per unit or per pack. Per pack, the per-unit cost is worked out for you.
steps.3: Leave Opening stock unticked. It is only for stock that was on the shelf when the system started.

quantity.tip: The cost price is what the profit reports are built on, and it is kept with this batch forever. A later delivery at a new price does not change it.

steps.1: Press Save delivery. The stock goes up straight away and the till can sell it.
steps.2: The delivery appears in the list under Received today.
steps.3: Repeat for each batch on the invoice.
steps.4: Put the new boxes behind the older ones on the shelf, so the soonest expiry goes out first.

wrong.title: If you made a mistake

steps.1: A saved delivery is never edited or deleted -- the stock history cannot be changed.
steps.2: A wrong quantity is corrected with a stock count: count that medicine, and posting the count books the difference with a reason.
steps.3: Tell whoever manages the stock straight away, while the invoice is still at hand.

wrong.warn: Do not book the delivery in a second time to "fix" it. That doubles the stock.

medicines.title: Adding new medicines
medicines.summary: Putting a new drug in the catalogue: the details that matter, the class, units, prices and barcodes.

check.title: First, check it is not already there

steps.1: Open Items and search by generic name, brand name and NIE number.
steps.2: If it is there but archived, change the status filter to Archived and restore it instead of adding a copy.
steps.3: A different strength or form is a different item: Amoxicillin 250 mg and 500 mg are two items.

check.tip: One item per product you sell. Two items for the same product split its stock, and the till will say it has run out when it has not.

steps.1: Open Items and press Add item.
steps.2: Generic name: the active ingredient, for example Amoxicillin. Brand name: what is on the box, if different.
steps.3: Choose the form (tablet, capsule, syrup...) and write the strength, for example 500 mg or 125 mg/5 mL.
steps.4: Leave the code blank and one is made from the generic name.
steps.5: Enter the BPOM registration number (NIE). It is how a product recall is matched to your stock.

class.title: 2. The drug class

steps.1: Choose the class printed on the packaging: Obat Bebas, Obat Bebas Terbatas, Obat Keras, OWA, jamu, herbal, a medical device or a consumable.
steps.2: Psikotropika and narkotika appear in the list only once the owner has switched them on in Settings.
steps.3: Choose a category too, so the item appears in the right lists, counts and reports.

class.warn: The class decides what happens on a return: obat keras, OWA, psikotropika and narkotika are always quarantined. Pick it from the box, not from memory.

units.title: 3. Units and packs

steps.1: Unit: the smallest thing you count and sell -- tablet, capsule, bottle, vial.
steps.2: Units per pack: how many units come in the box the supplier sends, for example 100 tablets per box.
steps.3: Deliveries can then be booked in by the box, and the system turns boxes into units.

units.tip: If you sell strips of 10 but count single tablets, the unit is tablet. Stock is always in units.

steps.1: Reorder point: the stock level at which the low-stock alert fires. Set it to what you sell before the next delivery can arrive.
steps.2: Suggested order quantity: how much to order when it fires. It is shown on the alert.
steps.3: Minimum shelf life: the shortest remaining life you want a delivery to arrive with, for example 180 days.

steps.1: Enter the sale price per unit in rupiah, for example 1500. Dots are fine: 1.500 means one thousand five hundred.
steps.2: Tick PPN exempt only for items your accountant says carry no PPN.
steps.3: The till charges this price. Changing it later does not change sales already made.

steps.1: After saving, open the item and add its barcode under Barcodes -- scan it or type it in.
steps.2: An item can hold several barcodes, one per supplier's packaging.
steps.3: Scanning an unknown barcode while receiving stock also saves it to the item you pick.

then.title: After saving

steps.1: The new item shows 0 in stock. That is correct: stock only comes from receiving a delivery.
steps.2: Book in the delivery on Receive stock, with its batch number and expiry.
steps.3: From then on it can be found and sold at the till.

then.warn: Never try to put stock on an item by editing it. There is no stock field on an item, on purpose.

import.title: Adding many at once

steps.1: Open Items and press Import.
steps.2: Download the template. Fill in the Data sheet, one row per medicine; the Guide sheet explains what every column wants.
steps.3: Do not rename the column headings on the Data sheet.
steps.4: Write dates as 2027-12-31. Barcodes keep their leading zeros because every cell is text.
steps.5: A row can also carry the stock already on the shelf: the batch number, expiry and quantity. That is booked in as opening stock.
steps.6: Upload the file. You see a preview first, with every row that has a problem and why. Only the rows that pass are saved when you confirm.

import.tip: For a new delivery, use Receive stock rather than import -- import only books in opening stock.

steps.1: Open the item and press Edit item to fix a name, class, price or level.
steps.2: An item you stop selling is archived, not deleted. It disappears from the till and the list, and its history stays.
steps.3: Restore it any time from the Archived filter.

suppliers.title: Suppliers and categories
suppliers.summary: Keeping the lists that deliveries, items and reports are sorted by.

steps.1: Open Suppliers and fill in the name, a contact person and a phone number.
steps.2: Saved suppliers are offered on Receive stock.
steps.3: The Suppliers report then shows what each one delivered and how much of it ended up written off.

categories.title: Categories

steps.1: Open Categories and type a name, for example Antibiotics or Vitamins.
steps.2: Choose the category on each item.
steps.3: Categories group the catalogue, let you count one shelf at a time, and split the sales and stock-value reports.

categories.tip: Name categories the way the shelves are laid out. Counting one category then means counting one shelf.

alerts.title: Alerts and expiry
alerts.summary: What each alert means, the daily routine, and what to do so nothing expires on the shelf.

steps.1: Expired stock on shelf (red): a batch has passed its expiry and still has units. The till already refuses it; it still has to come off the shelf.
steps.2: Out of stock (red): nothing left to sell.
steps.3: Expiring urgently (red) and Expiring soon (amber): a batch is close to its expiry. How close is set in Settings.
steps.4: Low stock (amber): at or below the item's reorder point.
steps.5: Dead stock: has not sold for a long time and is heading for expiry.

routine.title: Every morning

steps.1: Look at the count next to Alerts in the menu, or the four numbers on the dashboard.
steps.2: Open Alerts. The most urgent are always at the top.
steps.3: Take expired stock off the shelf first, and put it aside for disposal.
steps.4: For medicine expiring soon, move it to the front of the shelf so it sells first.
steps.5: For low and out-of-stock medicine, pass the list to whoever orders.

routine.tip: Alerts are checked automatically every day. The Refresh button checks again straight away, for example after a delivery.

steps.1: Mark as handled once it is dealt with, for example "already ordered". Your name is recorded on it.
steps.2: Snooze hides it for a few days, for example while a delivery is on its way.
steps.3: View item opens the medicine, with its batches and expiry dates.

critical.title: Red alerts cannot be snoozed

steps.1: Expired stock stays on the list until it is off the shelf and written off in Disposal.
steps.2: That is deliberate: expired medicine must never be forgotten on the shelf.

critical.warn: Marking an expired-stock alert as handled does not remove the medicine. Only writing it off does.

disposal.title: Writing off expired or damaged stock
disposal.summary: Recording medicine that is destroyed or sent back, so the stock and the loss are both right.

steps.1: Expired batches and quarantined returns appear by themselves under Waiting to be written off.
steps.2: A write-off is a loss: medicine that is destroyed, damaged or sent back to the supplier.
steps.3: It is not for correcting a miscount -- that is what a stock count is for.

steps.title: Writing it off

steps.1: Take the boxes off the shelf and have them in your hand.
steps.2: Open Disposal and press Write off on the batch.
steps.3: Check the batch number against the box. Enter how many are being destroyed.
steps.4: Write the reason (expired, damaged...) and how it was destroyed (incinerated, returned to supplier...).
steps.5: Choose who witnessed it, if anyone did.
steps.6: Press Write this stock off and confirm.

steps.warn: A disposal cannot be undone. Check the batch number and the quantity against what is in your hand before confirming.

why.title: Why it matters

steps.1: The Disposal record shows everything written off and the total loss for the last 30 days.
steps.2: The Expiry loss report shows which medicines keep being thrown away. Those are the ones being over-ordered.

why.tip: Keep any disposal paperwork (berita acara) with the disposal number the system gives you.

counts.title: Stock counts (opname)
counts.summary: Counting the shelf, comparing it with the system, and correcting the difference with a reason.

when.title: When to count

steps.1: After entering opening stock, to catch anything missed.
steps.2: Regularly, for example once a month, one category at a time.
steps.3: Whenever the till says something is out of stock that is on the shelf, or the other way round.

when.tip: One category at a time is far less disruptive than closing the whole pharmacy for a day.

steps.1: Open Stock count and press Start a count.
steps.2: Give it a name, for example "September opname -- antibiotics".
steps.3: Choose Everything or one category, and press Open the count sheet.
steps.4: The system writes down what it believes is on the shelf at that moment, batch by batch.

count.title: 2. Count the shelf

steps.1: Press Print the sheet, and count with a pen, batch by batch.
steps.2: Count every batch number separately, even if they sit side by side.
steps.3: Try not to sell from the shelf being counted until the count is posted.

count.warn: If something is sold mid-count, the system still records the sale correctly -- but your sheet and the shelf will disagree, and the count will show a difference that is not real.

steps.1: For each batch, type the number you counted and press Save.
steps.2: The difference from what the system expected is shown next to it.
steps.3: Every difference needs a reason, for example "damaged box found" or "miscounted at delivery".

post.title: 4. Post the count

steps.1: When every line is counted and every difference explained, press Post this count.
steps.2: The stock is corrected by the difference you found, with your reason attached, in the stock history.
steps.3: If the count was started by mistake, cancel it instead. Nothing changes.

post.warn: Posting cannot be undone. Recount any line with a large difference before posting.

reports.title: Reports
reports.summary: Reading sales, profit, stock and losses for any period, comparing them with the period before, and sending them to the accountant.

steps.1: Open Reports and choose a period: today, the last 7, 30 or 90 days, this month, last month, or your own dates.
steps.2: The Overview shows the main figures for the period. Each one is compared with the period before: an ▲ or ▼ arrow and the percentage.
steps.3: This month is compared with the same days of last month; last month with the month before; any other period with the same number of days just before it.
steps.4: The tabs at the top switch report without losing the period. A day is a day in the pharmacy's own timezone.

steps.1: The sales summary starts from gross sales and takes off discounts, returns and any VAT inside prices, down to net sales and the total collected.
steps.2: The daily chart shows this period with the previous one. Busy hours show when the till is busiest.
steps.3: The by-item table sorts by clicking a column heading and searches by name or code. ABC classes mark the items that make 80% of sales (A): never let those run out.
steps.4: By payment method: money in less money refunded. Check it against the cash count and the bank statement. Voided sales are left out of every figure.

movements.title: Stock movements

steps.1: Every unit in and every unit out per product, with who recorded it and the document behind it.
steps.2: Open a product to see each movement: delivery, sale, void, return, disposal or count.

movements.tip: This is the report for checking that what left the shelf matches what was rung up at the till.

steps.1: Gross profit: net sales less cost of goods. The cost is the one recorded when each batch was received, so a new price does not change last month's profit.
steps.2: Net sales are after discounts and exclude VAT, so profit never looks bigger than it is.
steps.3: Stock value: what is on the shelf right now, at cost, and how long it has left to sell.
steps.4: Expiry loss: what was written off and why. Suppliers: what each supplier delivered and how much of it ended up written off.

export.title: Printing and downloading

steps.1: Print: the report prints on A4 with the pharmacy name, the period, and who printed it. Every row prints, not only the ones on screen.
steps.2: Excel: one workbook with a Summary sheet and a sheet for each table. The figures are real numbers, so they sum as they are.
steps.3: CSV: the main table only, for Google Sheets or anything else.

export.tip: Excel is the easiest way to send the month's figures to the accountant.

history.title: Old sales history

steps.1: In Reports, press Import sales history and download the template.
steps.2: Fill in the Data sheet: one row per item sold, with its date, quantity, and price or total. The Guide sheet explains every column.
steps.3: Upload the file. You see the total, the period, and every row with a problem before you confirm. Days that already have sales at the till are flagged.
steps.4: History goes into the Sales and Gross profit reports but never changes stock. A wrong import can be withdrawn, with a reason.

history.warn: Only for days before this system was in use. Do not import sales that were already rung up at the till: they would be counted twice.

accounts.title: Staff accounts
accounts.summary: Creating an account for each person, choosing what they may do, and dealing with forgotten passwords.

create.title: Creating an account

steps.1: Open Accounts and press Add an account.
steps.2: Enter a username (lowercase, no spaces) and the person's full name as it should appear on receipts.
steps.3: Choose their language.
steps.4: Tick Registered pharmacist, with the SIPA and STRA numbers, for the pharmacist.

create.tip: One account per person, never shared. That is what lets every sale and every change be traced to who made it.

permissions.title: What they may do

steps.1: Start from a template: Cashier, Stock clerk or Manager.
steps.2: Then tick or untick individual boxes. The template is only a starting point.
steps.3: Each guide on this page appears for them only if they hold what it needs.

permissions.warn: Cost prices and profit, accounts, settings and import are marked as sensitive. Grant them deliberately.

password.title: The temporary password

steps.1: When the account is created, a one-time password is shown once.
steps.2: Write it down and hand it to the person. It cannot be shown again.
steps.3: They must set their own password at first sign-in. You never learn it.

password.warn: If it is lost, it cannot be recovered -- only replaced with Issue a new password.

steps.1: Issue a new password: for a forgotten password or a lockout. It signs them out everywhere.
steps.2: Suspend: for someone who has left. They are signed out at once; nothing they recorded is deleted, and the account can be reactivated.
steps.3: Sign out everywhere: if they stayed signed in on a shared computer.

steps.1: There is exactly one owner, and nobody can suspend or change the owner's account except the owner.
steps.2: Nobody can suspend their own account.
steps.3: If the owner is locked out, recovery is done on the computer the system is installed on.

settings.title: Settings
settings.summary: The pharmacy's details, receipts, tax, which screens are in use, and alert thresholds.

steps.1: Name, description, address, phone, NPWP and licence number.
steps.2: The name and description appear in the menu and on the sign-in screen; the name tops every receipt.
steps.3: The timezone decides when a day starts, and so which day a sale belongs to and the exact day a batch expires.

steps.1: The receipt language is set here, not by each cashier -- a customer gets the same receipt whoever serves them.
steps.2: The footer line is printed at the bottom, for example a get-well message.

modules.title: What is switched on

steps.1: Switch off screens the pharmacy does not use: returns, barcodes, PPN, narkotika, suppliers, categories, counts, disposal, import.
steps.2: Switching one off hides it from the menu. It does not delete anything already recorded, and permissions still decide who may do what.

modules.tip: Leave barcodes off until a scanner is plugged in, and narkotika off until the day you first stock them.

tax.title: PPN

steps.1: Switch PPN on only if the pharmacy charges it. Off means a plain nota with no tax.
steps.2: Choose whether prices already include PPN or are before PPN.
steps.3: Add the rate with the date it applies from. Old rates are kept, so a reprinted receipt shows the rate of its day.

tax.warn: Whether the pharmacy charges PPN is for the accountant to decide, not the system.

steps.1: How many days before expiry a batch turns amber, and then red.
steps.2: When unsold stock counts as dead stock.
steps.3: The daily email: a morning summary of yesterday's takings and what needs attention, once a mail server is set up.

steps.1: Allow sealed stock back on the shelf applies to over-the-counter items and devices only.
steps.2: Obat keras, OWA, psikotropika and narkotika are always quarantined, whatever this setting says.

demo.title: Demo data

steps.1: While the sample pharmacy is still installed, this section offers to clear it.
steps.2: Type the confirmation phrase to clear it. Accounts, settings, tax rates and the audit log stay.

demo.warn: Clearing empties the whole catalogue. Do it before entering your real items, never after.

historyImport.title: Import sales history
historyImport.subtitle: Sales from before this system, from the old books or the old program

counts.title: Counted in the reports
counts.body: Every line goes into the Sales and Gross profit reports on its date, with the breakdown by item, category, cashier and payment method.

stock.title: Never changes stock
stock.body: What is on the shelf was entered as opening stock. History is a record of sales only: it takes nothing from any batch and does not appear on the stock card.

today.title: Past days only
today.body: Today's sales and later go through the till. If the wrong file goes in, the whole import can be withdrawn.

historyImport.templateHint: Fill in the Data sheet, one row per item sold. The Guide sheet explains every column and has examples.
historyImport.fileHint: Excel (.xlsx) or CSV. Only the first sheet is read.
historyImport.previewSummary: {valid} of {total} rows are ready to import. {errors} rows have a problem and will be skipped.

figure.unlinked: {count} rows kept under the name in the file
figure.uncosted: Rows without a cost are left out of the Gross profit report

historyImport.duplicate: This file is identical to import {number}, which still counts. Importing it again would double its figures, so it cannot go ahead.
historyImport.overlapTill: {count} days in this file already have sales at the till. If the file holds those same sales, they will be counted twice.
historyImport.overlapImported: {count} days in this file are already in an earlier import. Make sure this is not a copy of the old file.
historyImport.errorsCapped: Showing {shown} of {total}. Fix these first, then check again.
historyImport.sampleTitle: Some of the rows that will be imported
historyImport.done: Import {number} is done: {lines} rows, {total} in total, {from} to {to}.
historyImport.seeReport: See it in the Sales report
historyImport.pastEmpty: No history has been imported yet.
historyImport.pastEmptyHint: After the first import it is listed here, and it can be withdrawn if it was wrong.
historyImport.withdrawHint: Every row of {number} is taken out of every report. The rows stay on record, with your name and the reason.

error.invalid_date: The date cannot be read. Write the year first: 2026-08-31.
error.date_too_old: The date is before 2000. Check the year.
error.date_not_past: Today and later dates go through the till, not through an import.
error.unknown_item_code: No item has this code. Check it, or leave it blank and fill in item_name only.
error.invalid_qty: The quantity must be a whole number above zero.
error.invalid_money: The amount cannot be read. Example: 15000
error.invalid_payment_method: Payment method not recognised. See the list on the Guide sheet.

guide.title: How to fill in the sales history import template
guide.intro: Fill in the "Data" sheet (the first sheet), one row per item in a sale. This "Guide" sheet is for reading only and is not imported.

how.1: One row is one item sold on one day. A receipt with three items is three rows with the same receipt number.
how.2: History is recorded for the reports only. Stock does not change, so do not import sales whose items still have to come off the shelf.
how.3: Past days only. Today's sales and later go through the till.
how.4: Do not change, delete or translate the column names in row 1. The system reads those names.
how.5: Every row needs date, qty, one of unit_price or line_total, and one of item_code or item_name.
how.6: Dates are year first: 2026-08-31. Money is a plain number in rupiah: 15000. Date and number cells from Excel are read too.
how.7: At most {max} rows per file. For more, split it by year or by month.
how.8: Rows with a problem are listed with their row numbers before you confirm, and are skipped. The same file cannot be imported twice.

guide.examplesIntro: Two receipts from 1 August and one row without a receipt from 2 August. Do not copy these into the Data sheet.
guide.paymentIntro: Write the code from the first column, or its name. Leave it blank if it was not recorded.

requirement.oneOf: One of the pair is required (see the next row)

date.accepted: Year-month-day, for example 2026-08-31. Must be before today.

receipt_number.accepted: Any text. Rows with the same number and date count as one transaction. Leave blank if there is none; the row still counts as sales, but not as a transaction.

item_code.meaning: The item's code in this system's catalogue.
item_code.accepted: An existing code, for example PARA001. If filled in, it must match. Fill in this or item_name.

item_name.meaning: The item's name as the old records have it.
item_name.accepted: Text. If it is exactly the name of one item in the catalogue, the row is linked to that item; otherwise it is kept under this name.

qty.accepted: A whole number above zero, in the smallest unit (tablet, bottle).

unit_price.accepted: Rupiah, for example 1000. Fill in this or line_total.

line_total.meaning: What was paid for this row in total.
line_total.accepted: Rupiah. If filled in, this is the figure counted (including any line discount). If blank: qty × unit_price.

unit_cost.accepted: Rupiah. Leave blank if unknown; the row still counts in the Sales report, but not in Gross profit.

payment_method.accepted: One of the codes in the table below, or its name. May be blank.

cashier.meaning: The cashier's name in the old records.
cashier.accepted: Any text. They do not need an account in this system.
